problemStatement.formal: \text{(Fano) For an estimate } \hat W \text{ of } W \text{ over } n \text{ uses of the BEC}(p):\quad H(W\mid \hat W) \le 1 + P_e \log(|\mathcal W|-1).
problemStatement.plain: The binary erasure channel (BEC) transmits each bit correctly with probability $1-p$ and "erases" it with probability $p$. Its capacity is $C = 1-p$. The parent gallery entry proves the *information-theoretic* supremum equals $1-p$ but takes the *operational converse* — "no reliable code can beat $1-p$" — as an axiom (`channel_coding_converse`). We want to prove that converse operationally via **Fano's inequality**, which bounds the residual uncertainty $H(W\mid\hat W)$ of the transmitted message given the decoder's estimate in terms of the error probability, and combine it with the data-processing / chain-rule bound to force $R \le 1-p$.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: BEC operational single-letter converse proved axiom-free (bec_fano_converse, bec_fano_error_lower) by specialising fano_converse_capacity; PR #34246.
builtItems: bec_fano_converse (ShannonChannelCodingBEC.lean): log 2 <= (1-p)log 2 + h(P_e), uniform Bool input; axiom-free
insights: For |alpha|=2 (Bool input) the Fano correction P_e*log(|alpha|-1)=P_e*log 1=0 vanishes, so fano_converse_capacity collapses to log 2 <= C + h(P_e) with no slack.
Substituting bec_capacity (C=(1-p)log 2) gives the sharp BEC converse p*log 2 <= h(P_e): capacity gap log 2 - C = p*log 2 is exactly the floor on Fano error entropy.
The asymptotic channel_coding_converse axiom is NOT needed for the single-letter BEC converse; the proved axiom-free Fano infrastructure suffices.
nextSteps: Optional: lift single-letter BEC converse to n-block operational statement (would discharge channel_coding_converse for BEC); needs I(X^n;Y^n)<=n*C tensorization + Fano over blocks.
Optional follow-up OQ: strong converse for BEC (error->1 above capacity) via blowing-up lemma.
